name: Premium Intro Text Logo Flicker
use_when: A branded intro needs fast premium motion for a creator, course, show, or social series.
The intro combines logo, proof footage, quote text, underlines, flicker, or 3D camera movement.
The production value of a reusable intro materially affects perceived quality.
avoid_when: A simple talking-head hook or proof frame would communicate faster.
The intro is not reusable or high-value enough to justify heavy motion work.
The motion stack would bury the brand, proof, or outcome line.
The project lacks a coherent brand style, font system, or proof material.

timeline_pattern.layer_rule: Use multiple text layers only when each layer has a job: brand, proof, quote, keyword, underline, or transition.
timeline_pattern.font_rule: A dense intro can mix fonts, but keep the roles controlled; about five useful font roles is usually enough.
timeline_pattern.flicker_rule: Use flicker, font changes, or rapid alternates as short accents, not as the main readability method.
timeline_pattern.platform_rule: Trim completed social intros to about 3-5 seconds and long-form/show intros to about 10-15 seconds maximum.

motion.rule: Animate the viewer's eye through one focus at a time: brand, proof, outcome.

keyframe_values.text_flicker_window: Use very short 3-9 frame flicker/font-change bursts only on accent beats and only if the final word remains readable.
keyframe_values.social_intro_duration: Aim for about 3-5 seconds for Instagram/Reels/social series intros.
keyframe_values.longform_intro_duration: Aim for about 10-15 seconds maximum for podcast/show or long-form brand intros.
keyframe_values.motion_blur: Use motion blur only when it makes movement feel premium without smearing text readability.
keyframe_values.three_d_camera: For Resolve/Fusion 3D-style intros, animate camera/brand objects over about 40-60 frames only when the opening still reads quickly.

sound.rule: Every flicker, logo hit, underline, or camera move should have either no sound or a frame-matched cue; avoid decorative unsynced whooshes.

captions.rule: Suppress ordinary captions during designed intro text unless accessibility requires both.

color.rule: Brand colors and text contrast should remain stable through flicker, blur, glow, or 3D camera movement.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use timed drawtext layers, overlay logos/proof clips, alpha fades, short flicker enable expressions, and pre-rendered underline/highlight assets. Export contact sheets for each focus beat.
implementation.remotion: Create reusable BrandIntro components with textLayers, fontRole, flickerFrames, underlineFrame, proofClip, cameraMove, and handoffFrame.
implementation.blender: Use 3D text/logo objects and a camera move only for reusable premium intros; render enough resolution for later crop/zoom.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use logo/text layers, flash/flicker effects sparingly, keyframes, compound clips, and beat markers; trim the compound to the final duration.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Essential Graphics text layers, nested sequences, opacity/position/scale keyframes, underline graphics, and SFX markers. Use After Effects or Resolve Fusion for 3D camera/multilayer intro work.

common_mistakes: Spending days on an intro that does not change viewer trust or perceived value.
Using too many fonts without clear roles.
Making flicker effects so fast or dense that the important words cannot be read.
Letting logo animation delay the proof or outcome.
Leaving the built intro longer than the final platform needs.
Using premium motion to compensate for weak brand, proof, or offer.
qc: Does the intro communicate brand, proof, and outcome in the intended order?
Is every text layer assigned a clear role?
Are flicker/font-change bursts readable at delivery size?
Does motion blur or 3D movement preserve text edges and brand clarity?
Is the finished intro trimmed to the platform duration cap?
Does the body start cleanly without a jarring style or audio handoff?
